test_cases.title: Monotonic Microsecond Time Source Returns Value
test_cases.setup: Build time_lib against the POSIX implementation and link the Google Test binary; initialize a juno::time::TIME_ROOT_T via juno::time::TimeInit using the POSIX tApi.
procedure: Initialize tTime via juno::time::TimeInit(tTime, tApi, nullptr, nullptr).
Call tTime.ptApi->Now(tTime) once and derive the microsecond value via tTime.TimestampToMicros(tNow.tOk).tOk.
Sample monotonic time twice with std::this_thread::sleep_for in between; assert second microsecond sample > first sample by at least the sleep duration.
Verify the Now call returns JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS and the derived microsecond value is non-zero after FSW startup has elapsed at least one microsecond.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Two consecutive Now()/TimestampToMicros samples with a 1 ms sleep between them differ by at least 1000 microseconds.

test_cases.title: Time Values Are Non-Decreasing Across Successive Queries
test_cases.setup: Build time_lib against the POSIX implementation and link the Google Test binary; initialize a juno::time::TIME_ROOT_T via juno::time::TimeInit using the POSIX tApi.
procedure: Capture an initial microsecond value t0 by calling tTime.ptApi->Now(tTime) and tTime.TimestampToMicros(tNow.tOk).tOk.
Loop at least 10000 iterations, calling Now and TimestampToMicros on each iteration to obtain ti.
On each iteration assert that ti is greater than or equal to the previous value t(i-1).
After the loop, assert that the final value is strictly greater than t0.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Across 10000+ successive calls, no microsecond value is less than its predecessor, and the final value strictly exceeds the initial value.

test_cases.title: Time Value Type Width Is 64-Bit Unsigned
test_cases.setup: Build time_lib and link the Google Test binary with <type_traits> and <cstdint> available.
procedure: In a Google Test, take the microsecond value type returned by tTime.TimestampToMicros(tTs).tOk (the .tOk field of RESULT_T<uint64_t>).
Use static_assert or EXPECT to confirm sizeof(decltype(tOk)) == 8.
Use std::is_unsigned and std::is_integral to confirm the type is an unsigned integral type.
Confirm the type is std::is_same<decltype(tOk), uint64_t>::value == true.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The microsecond value derived from TimestampToMicros is 8 bytes wide, unsigned, integral, and equivalent to uint64_t.

test_cases.title: Per-Call Time Query Returns Updated Values
test_cases.setup: Build time_lib against the POSIX implementation and link the Google Test binary; initialize a juno::time::TIME_ROOT_T via juno::time::TimeInit using the POSIX tApi.
procedure: Call tTime.ptApi->Now(tTime) and TimestampToMicros to obtain t0_us.
Sleep for at least 1 millisecond using std::this_thread::sleep_for.
Call tTime.ptApi->Now(tTime) and TimestampToMicros again to obtain t1_us.
Assert t1_us > t0_us and that (t1_us - t0_us) is at least 1000 microseconds.
Repeat the query a third time after another 1 ms wait and confirm t2_us > t1_us.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Each successive Now() call returns a freshly sampled, larger microsecond value, demonstrating per-call sampling rather than a cached constant.

test_cases.title: Time Query Latency Is Bounded And Non-Blocking
test_cases.setup: Build time_lib against the POSIX implementation and link the Google Test binary on a host capable of std::chrono::steady_clock.
procedure: Record a wall-clock start timestamp using std::chrono::steady_clock.
Call tTime.ptApi->Now(tTime) 100000 times in a tight loop.
Record a wall-clock stop timestamp using std::chrono::steady_clock.
Compute the average per-call duration as (stop - start) / 100000.
Assert that the average per-call duration is less than 50 microseconds (well below any blocking I/O or scheduling cost).
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Average per-call latency over 100000 Now() invocations is below 50 microseconds, demonstrating that the time query does not block on I/O or scheduling.

test_cases.title: POSIX Implementation Public API Equivalence
test_cases.setup: Build time_lib with the POSIX backend selected. The same LibJuno public header (libjuno/include/juno/time/time_api.hpp) used by the Pico2 build must compile and link in the POSIX build.
procedure: In a Google Test compiled against the POSIX backend, include the LibJuno public header juno/time/time_api.hpp.
Call each function reference in juno::time::TIME_API_T (Now, SleepTo, Sleep) through tTime.ptApi and verify each returns a successful status.
Verify the value derived from tTime.TimestampToMicros(tNow.tOk).tOk is a 64-bit unsigned monotonic microsecond value (reuse the type checks from SW-TC-TIME-003).
Confirm the test compiles and links against the same LibJuno header that the Pico2 build uses (no POSIX-only symbols leak into the public API).
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All juno::time::TIME_API_T function references are callable through the POSIX backend, return successful status, produce 64-bit monotonic microsecond values via TimestampToMicros, and compile against the unified LibJuno public header shared with the Pico2 build.

test_cases.title: POSIX Time Source Tracks Wall Clock Elapsed Duration
test_cases.setup: Build time_lib against the POSIX implementation and link the Google Test binary; initialize a juno::time::TIME_ROOT_T via juno::time::TimeInit using the POSIX tApi.
procedure: Call tTime.ptApi->Now(tTime) and tTime.TimestampToMicros to obtain t0_us.
Sleep for exactly 100 milliseconds using std::this_thread::sleep_for.
Call tTime.ptApi->Now(tTime) and tTime.TimestampToMicros to obtain t1_us.
Compute delta_us = t1_us - t0_us.
Assert delta_us is greater than or equal to 95000 and less than or equal to 200000 (allowing for scheduler jitter on the host).
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The POSIX implementation reports an elapsed delta within [95000, 200000] microseconds for a 100 ms sleep, demonstrating monotonic microsecond tracking equivalent to flight.

test_cases.title: Pico2 Implementation Hardware Demonstration
test_cases.setup: Flash a demo firmware onto the Raspberry Pi Pico 2 that prints time_lib microsecond values (via tTime.ptApi->Now and tTime.TimestampToMicros) over USB serial at 1 Hz for at least 30 seconds. Open a host serial terminal at 115200 baud and capture the output to a log file.
procedure: Connect the Pico2 board to the host via USB.
Flash the time-demo firmware onto the Pico2.
Open the serial terminal at 115200 baud and begin logging to time_demo_serial.log.
Reset the Pico2 and let the firmware run for at least 30 seconds.
Stop logging and inspect time_demo_serial.log.
Verify each printed value is a 64-bit unsigned microsecond count and that successive values are strictly increasing.
Verify the difference between the first and last printed value approximates the elapsed wall-clock time within 5 percent.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The Pico2 firmware prints a monotonically increasing 64-bit microsecond stream for at least 30 seconds, with the first-to-last delta matching the elapsed wall-clock duration within 5 percent.

expected_artifacts.name: time_demo_serial.log
expected_artifacts.description: USB-serial capture of Pico2 firmware printing time_lib microsecond values at 1 Hz for at least 30 seconds.
